methodology: Each of the 6 query templates is run against every persona in the split, producing one 'case'. The ranker sees only an OBSERVATION TRACE (declines with reasons, enjoyment reports, interest taps, occasional stated preferences) folded through the production `apply_decline`/`apply_enjoyment`/`ActivityEngagement`; graded relevance (0-3) is assigned from the persona's separate, richer BRIEF (hard constraints, stated tastes, stated avoids, decline history) that the ranker never receives. Two metrics that were true by construction are no longer reported here at all: `constraint_satisfaction@3` was `1.0 if top else 0.0` (because `filter_candidates` removes every hard-constraint violation before anything is graded or ranked) and `series_duplication_rate@3` was 0.0000 (because `_dedupe_series` always runs). Both are now unit tests on `activity_search` itself, where a regression would actually fail something. The headline family is `NDCG@1`, `HitRate@3 (rel=3)` and `slate_ndcg@3`, whose ideal is computed under the product's own one-per-category slate rule so a within-margin variety swap is not scored as a loss; graded `NDCG@3` is kept in the technical table. `P@3` and `MRR` count a grade-3 TASTE MATCH as relevant, not the neutral grade 2: 77.8% of the core kept pool grades >=2, so the old `P@3 (rel>=2)` measured pool composition. `context_rule_conformance@3` is a SEPARATE metric from `NDCG@3` (relevance), not a variant of it: relevance asks whether a listing suits what the persona asked for and has liked before, graded from a persona brief that is never told about the weather; `context_rule_conformance@3` asks whether the ranker's top-3 matches a declared rain/environment rule (`context_labels.py`). That rule intentionally restates the SAME premise `activity_search.py`'s own `context` factor encodes, so this metric is an implementation-conformance check -- it shows the factor is wired and behaves as declared -- NOT an independent judgement of whether that rule is a good idea, and its `no_context` delta must not be read as evidence for or against the rain nudge itself. See docs/adr/0003-relevance-vs-context-appropriateness.md.
not_user_truth: NOT_USER_TRUTH: every persona, listing and observation trace in this benchmark is a synthetic design artefact authored for this evaluation. No row here is, or is derived from, a real senior's data, preferences or history. Graded relevance is assigned by a documented rule applied to an authored persona BRIEF the ranker never sees (see `dataset.py`'s module docstring); it is a labelling convention, not a fact about anyone.
